messages:
maria: Heads up — planning a synthetic load run tonight to validate the revised backpressure thresholds on GPU pools in eu-west-1. Goal: confirm queue_depth soft/hard limits and admission reject behavior before we flip on the new policy. Need folks to watch dashboards and be ready to rollback routing if we see cascading evictions.

aj: Quick Q — what are the target arrival rates and tokens/s? Also is this hitting the shared batcher or direct per-model workers? KV cache warm hits will change effective load.

linh-ml: Recommend targeting model redwood-13b-quant for this test (it’s the most commonly used at scale). We should do a 3-phase run: 10m ramp, 20m steady, 5m spike. Include a warmup phase to populate KV cache or we'll conflate cold-starts with admission pressure. Kernel path differences may show on p95.

maria: Plan draft (short):
```yaml
plan_id: probe-2026-02-backpressure
region: eu-west-1
model: redwood-13b-quant
phases:
  - name: ramp
    duration: 600s
    target_qps: 1200
  - name: steady
    duration: 1200s
    target_qps: 1800
  - name: spike
    duration: 300s
    target_qps: 4200
admission:
  queue_depth_soft: 50
  queue_depth_hard: 250
  reject_mode: reject_after_hard
  allow_partial_batching: true
metrics_to_emit: [queue_depth, admission_rejects, tokens_per_sec, gpu_util, kvcache_hit_rate, p95_latency]
```
I picked numbers to push but not immediately risk total region outage. We’ll start at 2200Z if no objections.

jamal: Region note — eu-west-1 has limited A100 spare capacity this week. If the test pushes autoscaler too hard we might see cross-region spill to us-west-2. If that happens we should preemptively pause routing rather than let the fallback flood other regions. I can escalate quota if needed but that takes time.

ops-bot: loadtest-bot created plan probe-2026-02-backpressure (id: lt-87321). Use `/loadtest status lt-87321` to check.

aj: Dashboards to watch: infra/queue_depth (per-pool), infra/admission_rejects, model/tokens_per_sec, host/gpu_util, infra/sched_delay, caching/kvcache_hit_rate. Also check k8s HPA events for batcher pods — if HPA lags we get queueing.

linh-ml: Add a small sampling of model logits and output sanity checks every minute so we can detect quality regressions in case quantization or kernel fallback kicks in under pressure. Not just perf metrics.

maria: Agreed. Also: we should test two admission configs — current production and new proposed. We'll run the steady phase with prod settings, then apply proposed and do the spike. That way we can compare admission_rejects vs p95.

jamal: I'll be on standby for capacity toggles and will open a cloud ticket if autoscaler hits quota. If we see spill-over, I will trigger manual routing to dark pools.

devops: I'll be on-call for the run and monitoring pager.

maria: ok. small checklist: 1) lt plan created (ops-bot confirmed) 2) dashboards pinned 3) canary A/B compare captured 4) notify support -> done. If nobody screams by 2200Z I’ll kick it off.

aj: small extra: keep an eye on admission latency distribution. A few long-tail scheduling delays can indicate contention in the batcher KV locks, which looks like increased p99 but not necessarily higher queue_depth.

jamal: cost note — prolonged spikes cause extra spot eviction risk and double-billing on fallbacks. We should cap the spike to 5m as proposed.

maria: starting now (kickoff) — running ramp.

loadtest-bot: lt-87321 status: ramp phase started (target_qps=1200). Streaming sample logs to logs.redwood.internal/lt-87321

linh-ml: seeing kvcache_hit_rate climbing during ramp (good), p95 stable ~420ms.

aj: queue_depth trending up but under soft (peaking ~37). GPU util ~68%. No rejects yet.

maria: moving to steady in 2m.

loadtest-bot: lt-87321 status: steady phase started (target_qps=1800).

aj: steady: queue_depth ~65 now — above soft but below hard; admission requeueing observed (~1.2% requeues). p95 drifting to 520ms.

linh-ml: sampling outputs look sane so far. KV cache hit rate dropped a bit when we introduced a small non-prefetch workload, adding to effective load.

jamal: seeing HPA scale events. One batcher pod entered CrashLoopBackoff for a short time (OOM on large batch), recovered. Keep an eye.

maria: moving to spike in 1m. Confirm everyone ready to abort route if rejects > 8% sustained for 60s?

aj: ready.

maria: spike now.

loadtest-bot: lt-87321 status: spike phase started (target_qps=4200).

aj: rejects jumped to 12% within 20s, queue_depth hit hard limit 250 in several pools, autoscaler triggered cross-region fallback.

jamal: initiating manual routing pause to prevent us-west-2 spill. Pausing traffic to fallback pools now.

maria: aborting spike — stopping load generator.

loadtest-bot: lt-87321 status: aborted by maria. Summary: peak_qps=4100, peak_gpu_util=98%, max_queue_depth=250, peak_rejects=12%, duration=1200s. Full report: https://reports.internal/lt-87321

linh-ml: good catch. Proposed thresholds prevented total meltdown but we still saw significant rejects under spike. We should consider lowering hard limit or introducing dynamic shedding (per-tenant backoff) to protect critical customers.

aj: also worth tuning batcher memory headroom to avoid the OOM during spikes. If batch sizes grow uncontrolled we get instability.

jamal: I'll open a follow-up ticket for capacity/quota and a run in us-west-2 after we iterate config.

maria: thanks all. Quick retrospective in #eng-runtime in the morning. :thumbsup:
